reasoning: The only fully successful audit (deepseek-v4-flash) reviewed all 6 maintainer files and found no malicious code. The PKGBUILD uses a standard VCS source with a pinned tag, and the build/install steps are routine for a .NET application. The wrapper script simply sets an environment variable and launches the binary. The other reports resulted in 'inconclusive' solely due to tool/API errors (HTTP 400s and parsing failures), not because of any security concerns. The advisory report also found no issues.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused entirely by tool and API failures in the other models (HTTP 400 errors for qwen, parsing errors for openrouter/free), not by genuine security ambiguities. The single fully successful model correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed with HTTP 400 errors on .gitignore, .SRCINFO, and xivlauncher-rb.
openrouter/free failed to parse model responses for 0BSD and XIVLauncher.desktop.
learnings: Distinguish tool/API failures from security inconclusiveness: The audit tool should flag HTTP 400s and parsing errors as infrastructure failures rather than mixing them into the security verdict.

Free-tier model routing: The openrouter/free router selected models that failed to follow the required output schema, causing parsing errors. Enforce stricter output formatting or use more capable models for parsing.
